extracted.intended_audience: merchants, traders, market officials and customs officers (historical/Italian trade context)
extracted.subtask_description: A historical tariff/market manual listing unit conversions, city-specific valuations, packaging conventions, commodity prices, and quality standards used by merchants and customs officers to value and trade goods across Mediterranean/Northern European markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency exchange and coin valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: City-specific values and conversion rates for coins (e.g., florins, franchi, marco, foldi, ducati, rials) and how different coinages compare in each market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides many explicit conversions and relative values across cities: e.g., descriptions like 'in Parigi ... pagamenti a racbì e acojone ... 1 frco ... 1 fiorino' and tabulated examples comparing values in Genoa, Venice, Paris, London, Lisbon, etc. Guidance indicates that merchants must apply the city-specific coin valuations when computing prices or making payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit, weight and volume conversions between regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and conversion relationships among commercial measures (cantare, carica, tonnellata, moggio, tona, tomolo, cantara, libra, oncia) and how these units translate when moving goods between cities/regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text gives many cross‑city equivalences and examples (e.g., 'una carica ... toma ... in vinegia', cantare/tonnellata/cantare values in Candia, Genoa, Venice, Flanders, Alexandria). Merchants are instructed to convert local measures to the destination city's standard when valuing or selling goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging and container standards for liquids and bulk (barili, botte, botti)
rubrics_metrics.description: How barrels/containers are defined and counted (barili, botte, botte metrics) and when a container is considered a barrel or a different unit across ports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that a 'botte' may be counted as a certain number of barili or a unit (e.g., distinctions for malvasia, vino, olio in Candia, Domafeo, etc.), with examples of how many barili or cantare constitute a ton/tonnella in different markets; instructions affect pricing and taxation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commodity pricing and market valuation by city
rubrics_metrics.description: City- and commodity-specific prices (per cantare, per tona, per carica, per cantare grossa) for staples and manufactured goods, used to compute market value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous examples: prices for grain, wine, malvasia, olive oil, maiolica, textiles, iron, wool, etc., given for Milan, Genoa, Venice, Bruges, Flanders, London, Paris, Alexandria, Candia, Constantinople and others. Guidance: use the listed local price for valuation and adjust via unit/currency conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textile measurement, grading and pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for selling cloths and textiles (panni, velluti, drappi, tele, lana, filato) including unit-of-sale conventions (per tonello, per pefo), typical prices, and differences across markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists which textiles sell by tonello/pefo and gives sample prices in Bruges/Flanders/London/Paris/Bruges/Genoa, and notes on how finishing (bagnato, tinto, fregi) affects valuation. Also notes special treatment (e.g., some fabrics sold by 'cantare' or in 'balle').

rubrics_metrics.name: Spice and aromatic product quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative attributes required for spices and aromatics (pepper, cannella, chiodi (cloves), garofani (cloves/flowers?), noce, zucchero, capperi, etc.): color, cleanliness, aroma, absence of excessive dust/powder, size/wholeness and maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long, detailed prescribing language: e.g., pepper should have 'buon colore e netti' and 'poca polvere', 'garofani' should be 'buon colore' and 'affatto puliti', capers should be 'frefebi e verdi e con poco sale', nutmegs should be 'piene' not hollow, etc. The manual enumerates acceptable and unacceptable traits (dusty, broken, too green, overly bitter) for each spice, used by buyers to judge lots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leather and hide quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Desirable characteristics for various leathers (cuoi di bue, bufala, kid, etc.): color (nero/lucido, bruno), cleanliness, slimness, absence of wormholes or bad smell, proper tanning and finishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies preference for 'cuoi negro e lucido', 'pelle pulita e no crepa', small hairs (pelo piccolo), well‑tanned, not worm‑eaten, and other traits. Differentiates uses and desired features (e.g., for saddlery, shoes, hats), and how defects reduce value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemstone and precious-metal quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for gems and precious metal goods (rubies, emeralds, corals, goldwork): color hue and purity, clarity, size/shape, polish, and whether stones are treated or flawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include preferences for 'rubini ... buona mena e color', 'colore rofato chiaro', and guidance that certain hues or impurities reduce value; also instructions about desirable mounting and how to judge piece quality before purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commodity-specific packaging/content and product form standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards describing how certain commodities are typically packed, their standard forms (e.g., maiolica counts per cantare, weights of wool bales), and what constitutes a standard lot for sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives specifics such as how many maiolica per cantare or tona, what constitutes a carica of malvasia, how many pifa/barili constitute a shipment, and when a shipment is considered reduced/damaged (e.g., botte non barili). These conventions affect saleable quantity and pricing adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules and cautions against adulteration and false substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisories that certain goods must not be 'copied' or adulterated (e.g., pepper, aromatic goods), and that buyers should know differences among varieties and avoid accepting imitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States buyers must 'saper le differenze' and warns that some aromatic goods 'non si possono copiare': merchants should refuse adulterated or imitation goods and prefer known, correctly labeled varieties; the manual lists which products are commonly adulterated and cautions how to inspect them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market and fair calendar / trading schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates and timing for important regional fairs and markets where goods are bought/sold (lists of fair dates by city/region).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides many fair dates (e.g., fairs in Puglia, Foggia, Bari: dates in May, June, September, October; other fairs listed 'di giugno', 'di maggio', etc.). Merchants use these to plan travel, stock, and timing of transactions.
